bindings.label: 17-year-old male with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions
One week prior, he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved; he denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms.
He took acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before onset of the mucocutaneous eruption.

Physical examination showed afebrile status, normal vital signs including respiratory rate 16 breaths/min and oxygen saturation 97%; shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate; circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis; 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities; remainder of mucocutaneous (including palms and soles), cervical lymphatic, and cardiopulmonary examinations were unremarkable.
SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid test was positive repeatedly
Mycoplasma and other respiratory pathogen tests were negative
HSV and enterovirus PCR/serology and skin biopsy direct immunofluorescence results are not yet available
VZV PCR/serology results are not yet available
